samples_judged.question_text: The two parts are 91 and 4. What is the sum?
The dot is at 68 and it moves forward 10 numbers. Starting from 68, just count up 10 numbers. Which number will the dot land on?

(Large group of 30 bunnies) — There are 30 bunnies.
(Large group of 30 bunnies) — 30 more bunnies are added.
How many total bunnies are there?

(Large group of 68 chicks) — There are 68 chicks.
(Large group of 31 chicks) — 31 more chicks are added.
How many total chicks are there?

verdicts.reasoning: Every sample is an addition task; seeds 11 (30 + 54) and 118 (26 + 51) are bare number sentences where finding the total is the whole demand.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: Key convention is inconsistent inside this set — seed 11 keys the value '84' while seeds 42, 91 and 103 key option letters (C, B, A).

verdicts.reasoning: The set pushes right up to the boundary without crossing it: seed 78 is 94 + 5 = 99 and seed 103 is 68 + 31 = 99, and no sample produces a total of 100 or more.
Column by column no pair carries: seed 103's 68 + 31 gives 8+1=9 and 6+3=9, seed 118's 26 + 51 gives 6+1=7 and 2+5=7, seed 11's 30 + 54 gives 0+4 and 3+5. The whole set holds to this.

Three distinct model types are actually drawn for the pupil: a NumberBond with the whole left blank (seed 23), a NumberLine with the dot at 68 moving forward 10 (seed 42), and grouped-object EmojiPictorial items (seeds 91 and 103) — that is the variety the clause asks for.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: The emoji items render their groups as text labels — '(Large group of 30 bunnies)', '(Large group of 68 chicks)' — so nothing is countable at those magnitudes; the pupil must take the number from the sentence. No base-ten or place-value block model appears anywhere in the set.

verdicts.reasoning: Seed 23 bonds the parts 91 and 4, and seed 78 asks 94 + 5 — both set a one-digit addend against a two-digit one, which is this half of the clause.
Seed 11 (30 + 54), seed 64 (60 + 26 = 86, true/false) and seed 118 (26 + 51) each add two two-digit numbers, so this half of the clause is covered by more than one item type.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: Variety is thin here: 30 + 30 appears at seeds 57 and 127 and again as the emoji item at seed 91, so 3 of 10 samples reuse one pair. Seed 91 also offers '0' as a distractor for a total of two groups of 30, which no pupil reasoning would produce.
